# **West Coast Fisheries Participation App (`wcfishparapp`)**

[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)

**`wcfishparapp`** publishes the West Coast Fisheries Participation Survey as an
interactive county-level map. It covers four waves — **2017, 2020, 2023 and
2026** — and is built as a [golem](https://thinkr-open.github.io/golem/)
structured R package that ships a Shiny application.

The survey asks commercial fishermen in Washington, Oregon and California why
they fish, and how shifting opportunity and profitability affect their
communities. This app aggregates those responses to the county level.

## **Installation**

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("connorlewissmith/wcfishparapp")
```

## **How to run**

``` r
library(wcfishparapp)
run_app()
```

For development, `dev/run_dev.R` loads the package from source and launches the
app without installing it. The repository root also carries an `app.R` entry
point, which is what Posit Connect and shinyapps.io use.

## **What the app does**

### **Map tab** — `R/mod_map.R`, `R/map_config.R`

A single Leaflet choropleth drives every survey wave. The year is a control
*inside* the map rather than a separate tab, so the question you picked stays
selected as you move between years.

-   **Questions are listed by wording, not number.** The survey renumbers most
    items between waves, so the wording is the stable key; the selected year's
    own question number is shown underneath. 128 questions are offered, grouped
    into 14 topics.
-   **Values** are medians for ordinal statement questions, percent responding
    yes for yes/no questions, and counts for respondent totals. The legend says
    which.
-   **Hovering** a county gives the value and the number of respondents it rests
    on — a median from four responses looks identical to one from seventy
    otherwise.
-   **Clicking** a county opens census context: population, median income,
    percent college graduate, unemployment, and the USDA rural–urban continuum
    code.
-   **Difference view** maps one year minus another. It refuses when a wave did
    not ask the question, and warns when the two years are not measured the same
    way.
-   **Downloads**: the displayed data as CSV, and the map as a PNG. The PNG is a
    server-side `ggplot2` re-render rather than a screenshot of the Leaflet
    widget, so it does not need a headless browser on the deployment host. It
    always shows the full coast, not the current pan and zoom.
-   **"View the question as it was asked"** opens a crop of the printed survey
    instrument in a modal.

`mod_map.R` holds the drawing logic once. `map_config.R` holds everything that
differs between waves — the spatial data, question choices, bin edges, legend
labels and instrument crops — as one list entry per year.

> **Note for maintainers:** the label maps and image tables in `map_config.R`
> are source text lifted verbatim from the old per-year modules, so their
> references to the label vectors built in `06_prep_app_data.R` still resolve.
> Do not replace them with evaluated values — that silently breaks the link to
> the data pipeline.

### **Survey Documents tab** — `R/mod_survey_docs.R`

The full printed instrument for each wave, four pages per year, with zoom
controls. This is what lets a user check the exact wording behind a map.

### **About tab** — `R/mod_about.R`

Background on the survey, how to navigate the app, and acknowledgements.

## **Data**

The app reads a single prepared file, `data/fish_par_app_data.RData`, which
holds the per-wave spatial and tabular objects (`county_17_sf`, `county_17_df`,
and so on), the question lookups, the legend label vectors, and
`counties_all_sf`.

That file is **built elsewhere** — by `code/cleaning/06_prep_app_data.R` in the
**`fish_par_survey`** repository — and copied here. There is no automated link.
If the question sets or labels change upstream, copy the file across.

Since 2026-08-28 the map also carries the four **Holland indices** (fisher
identity, social capital, job quality, livelihood satisfaction — Holland, Abbott &
Norman 2020). They are not survey items: `fish_par_new/holland_ambio_2/16_export_indices.R`
scores every respondent on the measurement model fitted once to all four waves
pooled and writes `holland_indices.csv` into `fish_par_survey/data/raw/confidential/`;
each wave's cleaner joins it (`code/helpers/attach_holland.R`) and aggregates the
county **mean**. They share one bin scheme across waves (`"Hol"` in `map_config.R`),
a legend that says so, and a text panel in place of the survey crop
(`holland_index_note()`). Refresh order after any change to the survey database:
rebuild the database → refit/export in `holland_ambio_2` → `01`–`06` here → copy.

Two filters matter for reading the map:

-   Counties with **three or fewer respondents are dropped** during cleaning.
    The map still draws all 133 west coast counties underneath, labelled
    *"fewer than 4 respondents, not reported"* — genuine zeros and suppressed
    small samples are not distinguishable, so the map does not claim they are.
-   The **west coast restriction** is applied separately, in
    `code/helpers/assign_county_sf.R`. Across all four waves exactly one county outside
    CA/OR/WA clears the reporting threshold, so the restriction costs almost
    nothing.

## **Development**

| Script | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dev/01_start.R` | One-time golem setup |
| `dev/02_dev.R` | Adding modules, functions and dependencies |
| `dev/03_deploy.R` | Checks and deployment |
| `dev/run_dev.R` | Launch the app from source |
| `dev/04_snapshot_map.R` | Rendering snapshot harness |

### **Tests**

``` r
devtools::test()
```

`tests/testthat/test-mod_map.R` deliberately locks in several defects that were
once live — the half-point bin rule and the legend-to-band alignment are
regression guards, not style checks.

### **Snapshot harness**

`dev/04_snapshot_map.R` captures what the map actually renders — bins, legend
title, legend labels and instrument image — for all 297 question-and-wave
combinations. Use it around any refactor of the map:

``` sh
Rscript dev/04_snapshot_map.R before.rds
# ... make changes ...
Rscript dev/04_snapshot_map.R after.rds
Rscript dev/04_snapshot_map.R before.rds after.rds   # compare
```

A clean refactor produces no differences at all. The harness shims `colorBin`
and `addLegend` in the package's imports environment so the values come from the
module itself rather than from a reimplementation of its logic.

## **Deployment**

`manifest.json` describes the deployment for git-backed Posit Connect and is
**generated, not hand-edited**:

``` r
rsconnect::writeManifest()
```

Regenerate it whenever files are added or removed from `R/`, or the dependency
set changes. It currently pins **R 4.6.0** — the deployment host must have a
matching version available or package restore will fail.
